 Summary
 Bournemouth win 2-1 at Ipswich - Evanilson gives Bournemouth early lead at Ipswich ; Davis own goal makes it two before Clarke responds from spot
 Brighton 2-0 Brentford - Gomez stunner puts Brighton in front against Brentford ; Thiago sent off before Gross doubles lead from spot
 Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea - Le Fee penalty puts Sunderland ahead against Chelsea 
 Liverpool beat Palace 3-1 - Mac Allister gives Liverpool lead after Palace hit bar and have goal ruled out; Wirtz doubles lead and Isak adds late third; Nketiah with late penalty
 Close form Send us your views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Gary Rose & Sam Drury
 Most recent Most popular 'We are not in the title race' published at 16:23 GMT 16:23 GMT 
 FT: Brighton 2-0 Brentford 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross, speaking to Sky Sports: "No. We are not in a title race. But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season. You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results - we are not getting carried away yet. Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum. But we are really pleased to head into the international break like this."
 1 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'It wasn't a penalty' published at 16:19 GMT 16:19 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders, speaking to Sky Sports: "You know when you come here in this stadium it will be a difficult game and that was the matter tonight.
 "We knew it would be tough, we are disappointed we lost the game. At one point it went very fast from side to side. Sometimes we had to control.
 "With 11 behind the ball it is difficult to find the spaces.
 "How you do - good or not - it is a matter of staying together. The international break is coming so the lads can be calm in the head and when we all come back we need to be motivated to go again."
 On the penalty: "For me it wasn't a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him."
 31 36 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We were better team by far in first half' published at 16:14 GMT 16:14 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Crystal Palace 
 Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson, speaking to Sky Sports: "It's fairly tough to take. We come in at half-time as the better team by far. We created opportunities, we had one ruled out, hit the crossbar then our Achilles heel again, set pieces.
 "Obviously, go in 1-0 down but still full of belief and went after it first 15 minutes of the second half but just couldn't find a way through.
 "It's tough when you're chasing the game. We've been done by three counter-attacks really, which is tough to take.
 "We just couldn't put the ball in the back of the net and it's tough to take when things are going against you. Then every chance they seem to get goes in. That performance first half, if we play like that every game we'll pick up a lot of results.
 "We pick ourselves up and go again.
 "We went toe-to-toe and it's just so frustrating because you're looking for a lucky break, the ball to fall for you, which it did in the 93rd minute. It's probably not a penalty but if you get that in the first half, it changes the game completely.
 "It's about getting back up off the canvass. Togetherness is the key and we'll come back. We know we've got the players in there, we've done it before. Get one or two back and we can really kick on."

 Post published at 16:12 GMT 16:12 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Chelsea made 648 passes in this game compared to 292 for Sunderland. Too often the Blues were passing from side to side rather than getting at the Sunderland defence.
 118 24 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We were efficient in front of goal' published at 16:06 GMT 16:06 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Liverpool 
 Image source, Getty Images Liverpool attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz, speaking to Sky Sports: "It was a good game from us, really happy about the win and that's all that counts.
 "We were efficient in front of the goal. We didn't have so many big chances... well, maybe we did, I don't know, but it felt like we didn't so scoring three goals is always good. We defended quite well so a good team performance."
 On timing of the first goal: "It was really important, also with their disallowed goal. It was good momentum for us going into the break. It made the game a bit easier or more open for us.
 "It was a good moment to score."
 On his goal: "It was a great pass to Bradley [Barcola], into the space. The manager was talking so much to us to arrive into the box and I think we had three players in there. Luckily the ball came to me and I could score."
 On Liverpool's away form: "We are always confident because we know what a team we have and what quality we have. It doesn't matter if it's away from home but, for sure, we need to get more players in the home games."

 Regis Le Bris got it spot on published at 16:04 GMT 16:04 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 Gary Bennett 
Ex-Sunderland defender on BBC Radio Newcastle 
 Fantastic result. You’ve got to say from the off they were right up for it. 
 We lost Xhaka early in the game but credit to Ahoka, he came in and seemed like a seasoned pro. 
 You look at Brobbey, you play to his strengths and no team in the Premier League could handle him. The two centre-backs know they’ve been in a game this afternoon.
 The way Sunderland performed today, that’s what they were like last season.

 'You fear for Sage's job' published at 16:02 GMT 16:02 GMT 
 FT: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Mark Schwarzer 
Former Chelsea goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 I thought at times Crystal Palace were okay and created some chances. 
 They've come up against a good Alisson but it still doesn't deter from the fact they're bottom of the table 
 You fear for Pierre Sage's job, you feel it's running it's course and there's no way out in it's current form.

 Well, no one was appealing but Crystal Palace have been given a penalty!

 It won't change the result but that feels harsh.
